# Hermes Agent: New User FAQ & Troubleshooting Guide

## 1. General & System Architecture
- **Web Interface:** Launch the native web dashboard and browser chat via `hermes dashboard` (serves at `http://127.0.0.1:9119`).
- **Platform Support:** 
  - **Windows:** Native Windows 10/11 is a Tier 1 supported platform using `install.ps1`. Note: the dashboard `/chat` embedded terminal requires a POSIX PTY, so WSL2 is preferred if using that specific pane.
  - **ARM64 & Docker:** Multi-arch images (`linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64`) run natively on Apple Silicon and Raspberry Pi.
  - **Android/Termux:** Supported via `scripts/install.sh` using the dedicated `termux-all` dependency profile.
  - **NAS Bind Mounts:** For UGOS/Synology/unRAID permissions, use `PUID` and `PGID` (e.g., `PUID=1000`, `PGID=10`) to map container permissions to host storage.
- **Reporting Vulnerabilities:** Report security issues privately via GitHub Security Advisories or by emailing `security@nousresearch.com`.

---

## 2. Model Configuration & Providers
- **Local Ollama Overridden by Env Keys:** If you set a local `base_url` (e.g., `http://localhost:11434`) but have environment API keys set (like `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`), `provider: auto` might route to the cloud. Set `provider: custom` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml` to enforce the local endpoint.
- **Ollama Cloud:** Supported natively via `provider: ollama-cloud` using the endpoint `https://ollama.com/v1`.
- **Azure AI Foundry:** Run `hermes setup` to auto-detect `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL` or configure `provider: azure-foundry`.
- **Google Gemini:** OAuth CLI providers (`google-gemini-cli`, `google-antigravity`) are deprecated/removed. Use Google AI Studio with `GOOGLE_API_KEY` or `GEMINI_API_KEY`.
- **Claude Pro/Max vs. API Tokens:** Using an Anthropic API key always bills under API usage. To route through Claude Pro/Max subscriptions, authenticate via OAuth.
- **Vision Models on Custom/Local Providers:** Enable native vision payload forwarding by setting `supports_vision: true` in your model configuration.
- **Usage & Cost Tracking (`/usage`):** Local OpenAI-compatible backends (e.g., LocalAI) stream usage stats automatically as Hermes sends `stream_options: {include_usage: true}` by default.
- **Model Routing Policy:** Hermes does not support automatic complexity-based or cheap/strong model routing per turn (`smart_model_routing` was intentionally removed). Model selection remains explicit per session or via `delegation.provider` / `delegation.model` for subagents.

---

## 3. Messaging Gateways & Platforms
- **Interactive Setup:** Run `hermes gateway setup` to configure integrations (Discord, Telegram, etc.) interactively without editing `.env` or `config.yaml` manually.
- **Telegram Authorization:**
  - `allowed_chats` restricts *group chats*, not direct messages (DMs).
  - To authorize DM users, use `allow_from: "<USER_ID>"` under `telegram:` in `config.yaml`, approve DM codes via `hermes pairing approve telegram <CODE>`, or set `allow_all: true`.
- **File & Media Delivery:**
  - Inbound code and text files (e.g., `.py`, `.txt`) uploaded to Discord/gateways are injected into context or cached.
  - Outbound generated files and MCP `MEDIA:<path>` images are dispatched directly through Matrix (`m.file`), Email (SMTP attachments), Telegram, and DingTalk (Markdown image URLs).
- **Session Restarts:** Gateways default to `mode: none` for auto-resets. Unexpected crashes transition to `resume_pending`, preserving session transcript and history on reconnect.
- **Multi-Profile Gateways:** Run isolated multi-user setups (e.g., WeChat/Weixin) via multiple profile gateways or a single multiplexed gateway process.
- **Channel Personas:** Use `channel_prompts` in your config to assign distinct system prompts and personas per channel ID across Discord, Telegram, Slack, and Mattermost.

---

## 4. Agent Autonomy, Memory & Tools
- **Tool-Call Limits & Goals:** Single-turn iteration budgets default to `agent.max_turns: 90` (overridable with `hermes chat --max-turns <N>`). For long tasks spanning beyond limits, use `/goal` (persistent across turns and resumable via `/goal resume`).
- **Memory & Personas:**
  - User preferences and identity map to `~/.hermes/USER.md` (via `target="user"`).
  - Agent personality lives in `~/.hermes/SOUL.md`.
  - External memory plugins (e.g., YantrikDB, Honcho) are managed out-of-tree in `~/.hermes/plugins/`. For local Honcho instances, `base_url: http://localhost:8000` is accepted without a remote key.
- **Custom Tools & Plugins:** Develop personal tools as plugins placed in `~/.hermes/plugins/` and enable them via `hermes plugins enable <name>`. Core tools live under `tools/` and must belong to a toolset defined in `toolsets.py`.
- **Tool Optimization:** Small local LLMs (e.g., 4B/9B) struggle with large schemas (~45 tools). Run `hermes tools` to disable unused toolsets and reduce prompt overhead.
- **Observability:** Track execution chains and tool calls with the bundled Langfuse plugin (`hermes plugins enable observability/langfuse`) or inspect skill usage via `hermes insights` / `/insights`.
